blindSummary:
A self-governing state in free association with a larger partner state: male same-sex conduct was criminalised until 2023 (decriminalised by parliament); a deeply church-centred society; no legal gender recognition. A large gap from the associated state itself despite the association.

Underlying evidence base is that of the associated state, adapted for local conditions.
blindOutOfScope: A state in free association with a larger partner state; local deviations are noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: this public broadcaster's article is about the associated state's police hate-crime data (gender-identity-motivated incidents up 42% in 2023, spiking during a foreign anti-trans campaigner's visit), not this jurisdiction; included as associated-state context (this jurisdiction is a self-governing state in free association with that state).

NOTE: this public broadcaster's article is about a national self-survey of trans and non-binary people in the associated state (one in five threatened with physical violence), not this jurisdiction; included as associated-state context.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (April 2023): this jurisdiction decriminalised homosexuality - parliament voted to remove the 'indecent acts between males' provision (up to 10 years under a 1969 crimes act, never enforced); the amending act took effect 1 June 2023, described as 'a historic day'.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Oct 2020): decriminalisation plans stalled again - parliament deferred the crimes-bill report by three months; sex between men was punishable by up to 7 years; the nation was historically accepting of same-sex relationships but anti-LGBT sentiment arrived with colonisation.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Aug 2017): this jurisdiction moved to decriminalise - the draft crimes bill (drafted with the associated state's help) would remove two provisions (up to 7 years for gay sex, 5 for an 'indecent act', consent explicitly no defence); a member of a local LGBTI community organisation called the provisions 'draconian' colonial relics.

Public broadcaster's international service (Aug 2017): this jurisdiction's parliament began hearing submissions on the crimes bill replacing the 1969 act; a local LGBTI community group made a submission supporting decriminalisation.
